name: Jesse Frasure
notes: The DJ/electronic producer embedded in country — a Detroit-raised, EDM-trained programmer. The entry says the hip-hop/EDM vocabulary is "first-hand, not borrowed," and the defining contribution is stated as a construction order: "programmed-first construction with clap/snap backbeat, 16th hat loops, sampled kicks, and **disco-adjacent four-on-the-floor** on the dance cuts, with live cymbals and percussion overdubbed on top. Half-time bridges and hard beat drop-outs used structurally." So the kick carries a four-on-the-floor anchor set with `fourOnFloorInChorus` and the drop-out probability is the highest of any producer here, over the tightest quantize. The dance band is documented separately — "four-on-the-floor dance cuts at 118–128" inside a 65–135 window. Harmony is "I–V–vi–IV and ii–V–I pop turnarounds, plus static i7 funk vamps" with "a marked D♭ major presence," so the seventh share is high and `vamp` carries real weight; the funk vamp is authored as the one-chord family the entry describes — a *static* i, coloured to a seventh by the `extensions` block, with no second chord, because the entry names none. The bass is the reason no 808 block appears: "synth sub plus a funk-articulated electric bass with slides, ghost notes and syncopated 16ths — the most active bass writing in modern country," so the live bass is kept with a high `glideProb` and the lowest root-following of the modern producers here. `relatedGenres` is held to what the entry documents — "disco-adjacent four-on-the-floor" dance cuts, EDM training and "country/EDM radio shows" — which is a dance-pop/pop crossover claim; the entry never says house, so no house id is claimed. ⚠ Confidence is medium (research: medium-high). ⚠ The INFERRED parameters are the perc density, the four-on-the-floor share, the counter ratio and the 100 BPM centre — the entry quotes the 65–135 window and the 118–128 dance band but names no centre of gravity, so that figure is a choice, not a reading.
